A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the annihilation of dark matter particles in the galactic halos of our galaxy and of the Milky Way satellites can produce gamma rays with energies up to a few tens of GeV.
there are a few models which are consistent with both cosmic ray and gamma ray data, and that the cosmic ray data are not inconsistent with the gamma-ray data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the gamma ray signal from dark matter annihilations is likely to be detectable by the GLAST gamma-ray telescope.
, while the annihilation cross section of dark matter particles is constrained by the observed cosmic ray antiprotons, the cross section for annihilation into photons is not.
